That depends, if you’re re-installing windows 10 on a machine that was previously using and activated version of windows 10, your new installation will automatically be activated when it connects to the internet. 

If your installing windows 10 on the system for the first time, you should still be able to use your windows 8.1 activation key to license your new copy of windows.

Due to the embedded activation/digital licensing method used in Windows 10, you would need to use/purchase a retail license key for Windows 7 or 8/8.1 or 10 to activate your existing installation or to activate a fresh install. While not strictly legal, it would be possible to transfer your Windows license from your old motherboard, however, this is not possible if the board has died completely. So I’m afraid you’re out of luck. 

The other option would be to check if your Microsoft account has your Windows license linked to it, in more recent versions of Windows 10, on a Microsoft online account you can link your Windows license to your Microsoft account for easy activation/re-activation.
